review.scope: The three balancing-recovery steps and the exact teaching editions below. This is not a fresh review of every lesson or of private URECA notes.
calculation: Let phi:A->B be a unital ring map, V a unital left A-module, W a unital left B-module, and alpha:V->Res_A^B W an A-linear map.
B is a left B, right A bimodule with c.b=cb and b.a=b phi(a). Compatibility is (cb)phi(a)=c(b phi(a)) by associativity.
The pair map f(b,v)=b alpha(v) is biadditive by distributivity and additivity of alpha. It is balanced because (b phi(a))alpha(v)=b(phi(a)alpha(v))=b alpha(av). No factors are commuted.
The tensor quotient universal property therefore gives an additive map F_alpha:B tensor_A V->W. B-linearity and the two inverse identities remain obligations in the rest of the adjunction proof.
The cyclic-integer laboratory illustrates finite balancing examples. It does not prove the arbitrary-ring adjunction.
